findings: Owner request 2026-11-08: practice short questions for Chapter 1 in the style of the book exercise's short answer questions and of the Board 2-mark short question (self-check checkpoints with a short model answer), English and Roman Urdu. These are written from the chapter; they are not printed in the book. 72 questions, numbered 1-72, under the chapter's section headings: 1.1 3, 1.2 24, 1.3 6, 1.4 15, 1.5 5, 1.6 7, 1.7 12.

Coverage: base and derived quantities, the two steps of measurement, SI and its base and derived units (Tables 1.1, 1.2), the additional units SI permits, the SI conventions, prefixes (Table 1.3) and conversions, scientific notation, absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, digital instruments, significant figures (zeros, scientific notation, integers), the rounding rules (including the odd/even rule for a dropped 5), the addition and multiplication rules (worked examples 1.1 and 1.2 with changed numbers), the thumb rules (mean deviation, periodic uncertainty), limitations of significant figures, precision and accuracy, total uncertainty (sums, quotients, power factor), dimensions, homogeneity, derivation by dimensions and its limitations, and the boxes (Do You Know?, For Your Information).

Answers are 2-4 lines; numericals show brief working and every number was recomputed in Python. 3 comparison questions are answered with an answer_table (two columns). None of the exercise's short, constructed-response, comprehensive or numerical questions is repeated.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson); refs_verify.py reports 0 problems.

The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets; 8 Wazahat callouts are added after hard questions (Roman Urdu only).

Book errors avoided: no question uses the printed Moon-to-Earth light time, the µ symbol for the atomic mass unit, the order-of-magnitude chart positions, or the 0.1 cm / 0.5 A misprints in the 1.5 and 1.6 examples.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
